info.title: The TwentyThree API
info.description: API for the TwentyThree product, covering TwentyThree's Video Marketing Platform, TwentyThree Webinars and TwentyThree Personal. Some endpoints apply only for some of the products.

servers.description: Customer-specific API service url for the TwentyThree Platform.

post.description: Add a new call-to-action with default values for the given action type. The `type` must be a valid action type and `object_id` must refer to a video, category, workspace, or player. To customise the action's data after creation, call `/api/action/update`.

cache_time.description: If the reponse is returned from cache, this property details the cache time.

type.description: The type of the call-to-action. Must be a valid action type from `/api/action/types`.

object_id.description: The ID of the object the call-to-action is connected to. May be a video, category, workspace, or player.

fields.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

post.description: Permanently delete a call-to-action by its `action_id`. The action must belong to the current workspace. Returns an error if no matching action is found.

cache_time.description: If the reponse is returned from cache, this property details the cache time.

action_id.description: The ID of the call-to-action to be deleted.

fields.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

post.description: Exclude a call-to-action from being shown for a specific object. Set `remove_exclusion_p` to `1` to undo a previously added exclusion. Both `action_id` and `object_id` must belong to the current workspace.

cache_time.description: If the reponse is returned from cache, this property details the cache time.

action_id.description: The ID of the call-to-action to exclude.

object_id.description: The ID of the object for which the action should be excluded or re-included.

remove_exclusion_p.description: Set to `true` to remove a previously added exclusion.

fields.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

post.description: Include a specific object in a call-to-action, for example a video or webinar. Set `remove_inclusion_p` to `1` to remove an existing inclusion. Both `action_id` and `object_id` must belong to the current workspace.

object_id.description: The ID of the object to include, for example a video ID or webinar ID.

remove_inclusion_p.description: Set to `true` to remove an existing inclusion.

fields.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

get.description: List available call-to-action types and their configuration options. By default, built-in internal types are excluded; set `exclude_internal_p` to `f` to include them. Each type entry includes its name, description, position settings, timeline scope, and configurable options.

parameters.description: When `true`, built-in internal action types are excluded and only custom types are returned.

parameters.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

cached.description: Indicates whether or not the response is returned from cache.

get.description:
List calls-to-action for an object or retrieve a single action by `action_id`.
    Results can be fetched either for a video using a `photo_id`/`token` pair (no authentication required) or for any object using `object_id` or `action_id` (requires `read` permissions).
    Use `exclude_items_p` to omit disabled actions and `player_id` to scope results to a specific playback context.

parameters.name: object_id
parameters.description: The ID of the object to fetch call-to-action for. Using `object_id` requires `write` permissions.

parameters.name: action_id
parameters.description: The ID of the action to be looked up. Using `action_id` requires `write` permissions.

parameters.name: live_id
parameters.description: The ID of the webinar to be looked up. Using `live_id` requires `write` permissions.

parameters.name: photo_id
parameters.description: The ID of the video to fetch call-to-action for.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The corresponding token for the `photo_id`. The token may be explicitly time-limited in which case `expire` becomes a required parameter.

parameters.name: player_id
parameters.description: When retrieving a list from a player, specify the playback context by sending along a `player_id`.

parameters.name: exclude_items_p
parameters.description: Boolean to specify whether excluded/disabled actions should be omitted from the result. This parameter only has effect with `write` permissions and lookups by `object_id`.

parameters.name: exclude_pending_p
parameters.description: When `true`, actions whose associated video is still being transcoded are excluded.

parameters.name: exclude_internal_p
parameters.description: When `true`, built-in internal action types are excluded from the result.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

cache_time.description: If the reponse is returned from cache, this property details the cache time.

post.description:
Update a call-to-action's name, timing, and type-specific data fields.
    All type-specific option fields are required; file-type variables (image/video) may optionally be provided as file uploads.
    Use `time_relative_to` to control whether `start_time` and `end_time` are relative to the video duration.

cache_time.description: If the reponse is returned from cache, this property details the cache time.

action_id.description: The ID of the call-to-action to update.

start_time.description: Start time for the call-to-action, relative to `time_relative_to`. Use `before` to show before playback starts or `after` to show after it ends.

end_time.description: End time for the call-to-action, relative to `time_relative_to`. Use `before` or `after` for before/after-playback display.

return_url.description: URL to redirect to after a successful update. If omitted, a JSON success response is returned instead.

time_relative_to.description: Controls what `start_time` and `end_time` are relative to.

fields.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

post.description: Upload a file for a specific variable on a call-to-action. The `variable_name` must match an image or video field defined for the action's type. The action data is updated automatically after a successful upload.

cache_time.description: If the reponse is returned from cache, this property details the cache time.

action_id.description: The ID of the call-to-action to upload the file to.

variable_name.description: The name of the image or video variable on the action type to populate with the uploaded file.

fields.description: An optional, comma-separated list of fields to return in the API response. Default behaviour is to return all properties.

get.description:
Get a session access token, which can in turn be used to sign a user's session using `/api/session-redeem-token`. The return token must be used within 15 minutes.

    This procedure is designed to work alongside the Single sign-on or Paywall option in the site's security settings. When this option is selected, all visitors (not logged-in users) must be redirected to the site through this procedure in order to gain access to the site's content. This allows the developer full control of who is allowed in, and it is usually used for intranet sites or for sites behind a paywall.

    A session expires when it hasn't been used for 30 minutes. After this, the user must have his or her session re-signed.

    Whenever possible, you should make sure to include `email` and `full_name` in your request.

    You can configure remote log-in and log-out pages when enabling the SSO option in the TwentyThree backend, specifically if you you want to redirect un-authenticated users to a certain login page. This page should be designed to log in and authenticate users through your prefered identity system - and then delegate access to the client through the `get-token`/`redeem-token` chain. Similarly, you can define a link where the user is redirected to when logging out.

    By default, this method only gains the redirected user access to the site's front-end with published content from the site. In configuring SSO though, you can choose to Allow back-end login as well. This means that clients being authenticated with an e-mail address already set up with a full user account will also be logged in to the back-end through SSO.

This endpoint supports an extra set of parameters designed to support resumable/chunked upload and to work with Resumable.js, an open sourced JavaScript library for providing multiple simultaneous, stable, fault-tolerant and resumable uploads via the HTML5 File API released by TwentyThree.

To handle the state of upload chunks, a number of extra parameters are sent along with such requests:

* `resumableChunkNumber`: The index of chunk in the current upload. First chunk is 1 (no base-0 counting here).
* `resumableChunkSize`: The chunk size in bytes.
* `resumableTotalSize`: The total file size in bytes.
